d-local-outside-home:D2:10. **D2: what does a Stop drain?** Answered 2026-10-20 (the owner asked for advice and the controller decided, with reasons): only `wake:true` messages. `wake` is the sender's permission to start a turn on an idle recipient, so letting a `wake:false` message start one at Stop would empty the flag of meaning and let ordinary mail make an agent work while nobody asked; it keeps a person as the brake. The cost: an idle agent sees a `wake:false` message late, at its next tool call or next prompt, and the delivery report says so; a sender who needs it read now sets `wake`. The panel recommended the other option (drain everything at Stop, bounded) for an honest delivery report; the delivery report here is just worded to say what really happens.
